dangerAreas.name: Spadeadam EW Range
dangerAreas.description: UK's largest electronic warfare tactics range — 9,000 acres of Cumbrian moorland. Fast jets from NATO nations train in low-level EW, SEAD and drone-swarm trials. The only mainland UK site where practice bombs can still be dropped.
dangerAreas.aircraft: Typhoon, F-35, NATO allied fast jets
dangerAreas.nearestTowns: Brampton (8mi SE), Haltwhistle (9mi SE), Carlisle (18mi SW)

dangerAreas.name: Otterburn Training Area
dangerAreas.description: Largest army live-firing area in England — 23,000 acres of Northumberland moorland. Artillery, mortar and armoured vehicle live firing.
dangerAreas.nearestTowns: Otterburn (1mi S), Elsdon (4mi SE), Bellingham (8mi E)

dangerAreas.name: Donna Nook Air Weapons Range
dangerAreas.description: Lincolnshire coast air-to-ground weapons range. Used by RAF Coningsby and visiting NATO aircraft for live ordnance practice.
dangerAreas.nearestTowns: North Somercotes (2mi SW), Louth (10mi W), Grimsby (16mi N)

dangerAreas.name: Holbeach Air Weapons Range
dangerAreas.description: Air-to-ground range over The Wash foreshore. One of the most active air weapons ranges in the UK, shared by RAF and USAF aircraft.
dangerAreas.nearestTowns: Holbeach (8mi SW), Long Sutton (7mi SW), Spalding (15mi W)

dangerAreas.name: Salisbury Plain — Larkhill (North)
dangerAreas.description: Northern Salisbury Plain Training Area centred on Larkhill Garrison. Continuous live artillery and mortar firing. Largest military training estate in the UK at ~38,000 acres.
dangerAreas.aircraft: Apache, Wildcat, Lynx (HELARM/CAS), Army Air Corps fixed-wing
dangerAreas.nearestTowns: Amesbury (4mi SE), Tidworth (5mi E), Devizes (9mi NW)

dangerAreas.name: Salisbury Plain — West (Imber)
dangerAreas.description: Imber village and western Plain — evacuated in 1943 and never returned to civilian use. Tanks and armoured vehicles manoeuvre over open downland.
dangerAreas.nearestTowns: Warminster (3mi W), Westbury (4mi NW), Trowbridge (8mi NW)

dangerAreas.name: Salisbury Plain — East (Tidworth/Ludgershall)
dangerAreas.description: Eastern training area around Tidworth Garrison. Armoured and infantry combined-arms training. Frequent helicopter operations.
dangerAreas.nearestTowns: Tidworth (1mi N), Ludgershall (2mi SE), Andover (9mi SE)
dangerAreas.polygonSource: UK AIP ENR 5.1 (YAIXM) D126 BULFORD — 13 pts

dangerAreas.name: Porton Down / Porton Ranges
dangerAreas.description: Science and Technology Laboratory (Dstl) and associated ranges east of Salisbury. Research into CBRN defence.
dangerAreas.aircraft: Surveillance and ISR drones, helicopter support
dangerAreas.nearestTowns: Amesbury (4mi W), Salisbury (6mi SW), Andover (12mi NE)

dangerAreas.name: Dartmoor Training Area
dangerAreas.description: Okehampton Military Camp and Dartmoor firing ranges. Used by infantry and Royal Marines for live firing and field exercises.
dangerAreas.nearestTowns: Okehampton (2mi N), Tavistock (10mi SW), Exeter (20mi E)

dangerAreas.name: Davidstow Moor / Bodmin Training Area
dangerAreas.description: Army training area on north Bodmin Moor. Used for infantry manoeuvre and helicopter underslung-load training.
dangerAreas.nearestTowns: Camelford (4mi W), Bodmin (12mi S), Launceston (9mi E)

dangerAreas.name: Plymouth Sound / Wembury Bay
dangerAreas.description: Naval firing range off Plymouth Sound and Wembury Bay. Used by HMNB Devonport surface ships and submarines for gunnery practice.
dangerAreas.nearestTowns: Plymouth (3mi NW), Plymstock (2mi N), Modbury (6mi E)

dangerAreas.name: Cowden Air Weapons Range
dangerAreas.description: Coastal Yorkshire air-to-ground range on the Holderness coast. Used for practice bomb delivery and strafing.
dangerAreas.nearestTowns: Aldbrough (4mi S), Hornsea (5mi N), Beverley (15mi W)

dangerAreas.name: Catterick Training Area
dangerAreas.description: Catterick Garrison live firing on Feldom and Bellerby ranges. Used by infantry, armoured reconnaissance and signals units.
dangerAreas.nearestTowns: Richmond (4mi E), Leyburn (6mi W), Catterick (5mi E)

dangerAreas.name: Warcop Training Area
dangerAreas.description: Army live-firing range in the Eden Valley, Cumbria. Artillery and mortar firing; significant noise impact in the Brough and Kirkby Stephen area.
dangerAreas.nearestTowns: Brough (3mi N), Appleby (5mi SW), Kirkby Stephen (7mi SE)

dangerAreas.name: Stanford Training Area (STANTA)
dangerAreas.description: Stanford Training Area — 30,000 acres of Breckland heath. Six abandoned villages cleared in 1942. Live firing, FIBUA training and brigade-level exercises.
dangerAreas.nearestTowns: Mundford (3mi E), Watton (8mi NE), Thetford (8mi SE)

dangerAreas.name: The Wash Danger Area
dangerAreas.description: Offshore danger area over The Wash — used as a weapons range by aircraft from RAF Marham and USAF Lakenheath/Mildenhall.
dangerAreas.nearestTowns: King's Lynn (8mi S), Hunstanton (10mi NW), Spalding (20mi SW)

dangerAreas.name: Lydd / Romney Marsh Ranges
dangerAreas.description: Lydd Army Training Centre on Romney Marsh — live small arms, medium machine gun and anti-tank weapons firing.
dangerAreas.aircraft: Army Air Corps light aircraft, occasional Wildcat
dangerAreas.nearestTowns: Lydd (1mi N), New Romney (4mi N), Rye (8mi SW)

dangerAreas.name: Hythe / Lympne Ranges
dangerAreas.description: Small Arms Ranges at Hythe — used by Army and Ministry of Defence Police for small arms qualification.
dangerAreas.nearestTowns: Hythe (1mi E), Folkestone (5mi E), Ashford (10mi N)

dangerAreas.name: Orfordness / Shingle Street
dangerAreas.description: Former weapons development site on the Suffolk coast. Offshore shingle has residual ordnance from decades of test firings.
dangerAreas.nearestTowns: Orford (2mi W), Woodbridge (12mi N), Aldeburgh (6mi N)

dangerAreas.name: Redesdale Training Area
dangerAreas.description: Army training area in the Redesdale valley. Artillery and small arms live firing; tank manoeuvres on Redesdale Common.
dangerAreas.nearestTowns: Otterburn (2mi SE), Bellingham (8mi E), Jedburgh (16mi N)

dangerAreas.name: Nesscliffe Training Area
dangerAreas.description: Infantry training area in Shropshire used by 143 (West Midlands) Brigade. Helicopter activity for air assault exercises.
dangerAreas.nearestTowns: Nesscliffe (0.5mi E), Shrewsbury (9mi SE), Oswestry (8mi NW)

dangerAreas.name: Eskmeals Proof & Experimental Establishment
dangerAreas.description: MOD Eskmeals — armament proof and experimental range on the Cumbrian coast. Propellant and explosive research, rocket motor testing.
dangerAreas.nearestTowns: Waberthwaite (1mi N), Ravenglass (3mi N), Millom (5mi S)

matzs.name: RAF Leeming MATZ
matzs.description: Active flying training base hosting No. 6 FTS and Qatar Emiri Air Force Hawk training. Significant circuit traffic throughout the day.
matzs.nearestTowns: Northallerton (4mi N), Bedale (3mi SE), Leyburn (8mi W)

matzs.name: RAF Coningsby MATZ
matzs.description: Primary Typhoon base and home of 29(R) Sqn OCU. QRA-South 24/7. Very high jet tempo.
matzs.nearestTowns: Coningsby (1mi W), Horncastle (5mi NE), Sleaford (12mi SW)

matzs.name: RAF Marham MATZ
matzs.description: Only operational RAF F-35B base. Home of 617 Sqn and 809 NAS. QRA-South responsibility.
matzs.nearestTowns: Marham (1mi E), King's Lynn (16mi NE), Swaffham (8mi SE)

matzs.name: RAF Waddington MATZ
matzs.description: ISTAR hub. Home of RC-135W Rivet Joint and E-7A Wedgetail (incoming).
matzs.nearestTowns: Waddington (0.5mi W), Lincoln (5mi N), Newark (20mi SE)

matzs.name: RAF Cranwell MATZ
matzs.description: RAF College — initial officer training and advanced fixed-wing flying training.
matzs.aircraft: Grob G120TP Prefect T1, Grob Tutor T1
matzs.nearestTowns: Cranwell (1mi NE), Sleaford (6mi SE), Grantham (12mi S)

matzs.name: RAF Lakenheath MATZ (USAF 48th FW)
matzs.description: Largest USAF base in the UK. F-15E and F-35A generate constant jet traffic. Occasional supersonic operations over The Wash.
matzs.aircraft: F-35A Lightning II, F-15E Strike Eagle
matzs.nearestTowns: Brandon (6mi S), Thetford (10mi SE), Ely (18mi S)

matzs.name: RAF Brize Norton MATZ
matzs.description: UK's largest RAF station — strategic air transport hub. C-17, A400M and Voyager generate continuous heavy transport traffic.
matzs.nearestTowns: Carterton (2mi NE), Witney (4mi E), Burford (4mi SE)

matzs.name: RAF Odiham MATZ
matzs.description: Home of the Chinook Force — entire RAF Chinook fleet. Frequent low-level Chinook transits across southern England.
matzs.nearestTowns: Hook (4mi N), Fleet (6mi NE), Basingstoke (8mi NW)

matzs.name: RAF Shawbury MATZ
matzs.description: Defence Helicopter Flying School. Constant helicopter circuit traffic including night flying.
matzs.nearestTowns: Shawbury (1mi E), Shrewsbury (9mi SW), Market Drayton (7mi NE)

matzs.name: RAF Northolt MATZ
matzs.description: RAF's London airfield and VIP/government transport hub. Royal Family flights and ministerial transport.
matzs.nearestTowns: Ruislip (2mi E), Uxbridge (2mi SE), Harrow (5mi NE)

matzs.name: RAF Benson MATZ
matzs.description: Home of No. 28 Squadron Puma HC2. Supports VIP transport for the Royal Household.
matzs.nearestTowns: Benson (1mi W), Wallingford (3mi N), Didcot (6mi N)

matzs.name: RNAS Yeovilton MATZ
matzs.description: Royal Navy's primary fast jet and helicopter base. Home of 809 NAS (F-35B) and Wildcat/Merlin force.
matzs.nearestTowns: Yeovil (6mi E), Ilchester (2mi NE), Taunton (12mi W)

matzs.name: RNAS Culdrose MATZ
matzs.description: Largest helicopter base in Europe. Home of the Merlin HM2 anti-submarine force.
matzs.nearestTowns: Helston (2mi N), Falmouth (8mi NE), Penzance (14mi W)

matzs.name: MoD Boscombe Down MATZ
matzs.description: Home of the Empire Test Pilots' School (ETPS). Experimental aircraft flights — almost any type may be encountered.
matzs.aircraft: Test aircraft of all types, UAVs
matzs.nearestTowns: Amesbury (3mi NW), Salisbury (8mi SW), Andover (10mi N)

matzs.name: RAF Fairford MATZ
matzs.description: USAF Forward Operating Location. Hosts B-2 and B-52 strategic bombers during exercises and RIAT annually.
matzs.nearestTowns: Fairford (1mi E), Lechlade (3mi E), Cirencester (8mi N)

matzs.name: RAF Linton-on-Ouse MATZ
matzs.description: Former RAF flying training station — closed 2023, now gliding club. Residual light aviation activity.
matzs.nearestTowns: Linton-on-Ouse (0.5mi E), Boroughbridge (5mi NE), York (10mi SE)

matzs.name: RAF Wittering MATZ
matzs.description: Home of No. 1 Air Mobility Wing. Puma HC2 and Chinook HC6 operations.
matzs.nearestTowns: Stamford (3mi N), Peterborough (9mi NE), Corby (14mi S)

matzs.name: RAF Mildenhall MATZ (USAF 100th ARW)
matzs.description: Home of USAF 100th Air Refueling Wing — KC-135R Stratotankers. Also houses USAF Special Operations.
matzs.nearestTowns: Mildenhall (1mi E), Bury St Edmunds (13mi SW), Thetford (12mi W)

matzs.name: RAF Honington MATZ
matzs.description: Home of the RAF Regiment Depot. Occasional Chinook/Puma force protection exercises.
matzs.nearestTowns: Honington (0.5mi S), Thetford (9mi E), Bury St Edmunds (9mi SE)

matzs.name: RAF Digby MATZ
matzs.description: RAF intelligence/signals station. Occasional light aircraft; primarily a ground station.
matzs.nearestTowns: Digby (0.5mi S), Sleaford (7mi W), Lincoln (14mi N)

matzs.name: RAF Barkston Heath MATZ
matzs.description: Satellite airfield of RAF Cranwell. Busy with piston-engine trainer aircraft; used for Red Arrows work-up.
matzs.aircraft: Grob Prefect T1, Grob Tutor T1
matzs.nearestTowns: Cranwell (4mi NW), Grantham (6mi S), Sleaford (8mi W)

matzs.name: RAF Halton MATZ
matzs.description: RAF Training Command technical training establishment. Limited helicopter use for exercises.
matzs.nearestTowns: Wendover (2mi S), Aylesbury (4mi E), Tring (4mi NE)

matzs.name: Kemble / Cotswold Airport MATZ
matzs.description: Former RAF Kemble. Hosts Global Aviation engineering, private operators and Cotswold Flying Club. Former Red Arrows engineering base.
matzs.nearestTowns: Kemble (0.5mi N), Cirencester (4mi N), Tetbury (5mi SW)

lfas.name: Low Flying Area 17 — Lake District & Yorkshire Dales
lfas.description: One of the UK's most active low flying areas. Military aircraft may fly at 250ft AGL. Fast jet transits through Wensleydale, Swaledale and Mallerstang are regularly observed.
lfas.aircraft: Typhoon, F-35, Hawk, NATO fast jets, support helicopters

dailyFlights.note: Sorties distributed across the whole LFA; individual locations experience fewer. Higher end reflects peak summer training season.
dailyFlights.sourceLabel: MOD Low Flying Statistics 2022–23 (HC Written Answer 18 Jan 2024); LFA17 among the three highest-activity English LFAs

lfas.name: Low Flying Area 20(T) — Anglo-Scottish Border
lfas.description: High-intensity tactical training area straddling the Anglo-Scottish border. Air combat manoeuvring and tactical formation flying. Altitude as low as 100ft in certain corridors.

dailyFlights.note: LFA20(T) is a tactical sub-area; sorties concentrated in specific corridors rather than spread evenly.
dailyFlights.sourceLabel: MOD Low Flying Statistics (annual HC Written Answers); tactical area with concentrated high-intensity usage

lfas.name: Low Flying Area 16 — Pennines & Peak District
lfas.description: Covers the central and southern Pennines including the Peak District. Fast jets use the valleys of Wharfedale, Airedale and Ribblesdale for low-level navigation training.

dailyFlights.note: Activity concentrated in the major valleys; ridgeline and plateau areas see fewer overflights.
dailyFlights.sourceLabel: MOD Low Flying Statistics (annual HC Written Answers); Pennines/Peak District medium-activity area

lfas.name: Low Flying Area 18 — North Yorkshire Moors
lfas.description: Covers the North Yorkshire Moors National Park. Low-level east–west transit routes used frequently by RAF Leeming and RAF Coningsby aircraft.

dailyFlights.note: Lower activity than LFA17; mainly transit and navigation sorties rather than sustained area training.
dailyFlights.sourceLabel: MOD Low Flying Statistics (annual HC Written Answers); N Yorks Moors lower-activity area supplemented by Leeming/Linton circuit traffic

lfas.name: Low Flying Area 7 — Welsh Marches & West Midlands
lfas.description: Covers Shropshire, Herefordshire and the Welsh Marches. Used by support helicopter units from RAF Shawbury and RAF Odiham for low-level navigation.
lfas.aircraft: Chinook HC6, Puma HC2, Merlin HC4, Juno/Jupiter HT1

dailyFlights.note: Predominantly helicopter sorties from RAF Shawbury (flying training school); daily training circuits supplement cross-country navigation sorties.
dailyFlights.sourceLabel: MOD Low Flying Statistics (annual HC Written Answers); RAF Shawbury published flying hours (gov.uk); Welsh Marches consistently high helicopter activity

lfas.name: Low Flying Area 1 — Southwest Peninsula
lfas.description: Covers Devon and Cornwall including Exmoor, Dartmoor and Bodmin Moor. Used by RNAS Culdrose and Yeovilton for maritime helicopter training.
lfas.aircraft: Merlin HM2, Wildcat HMA2, F-35B, Typhoon

dailyFlights.note: Mix of maritime helicopter training (Culdrose/Yeovilton) and occasional fast jet transits. Coastal areas see higher activity than inland.
dailyFlights.sourceLabel: MOD Low Flying Statistics (annual HC Written Answers); RNAS Culdrose annual report; Yeovilton Station Notice published flying rates

lfas.name: Low Flying Area 3 — East Anglia
lfas.description: Dominated by USAF operations from Lakenheath and Mildenhall. F-15E and F-35A aircraft conduct low-level navigation over the Brecks and coastal marshes.
lfas.aircraft: F-35A, F-15E Strike Eagle, KC-135R, RC-135W

dailyFlights.note: USAF figures are not published in MOD statistics; range derived from 48th FW published sortie rates (approx 6,000–8,000 sorties/year) and the fraction conducted at low level.
dailyFlights.sourceLabel: 48th Fighter Wing public affairs releases; MOD Low Flying Statistics (for RAF component); USAF EUCOM posture statements

lfas.name: Low Flying Area 8 — Midlands (Shropshire/Staffordshire)
lfas.description: Covers Shropshire, Staffordshire and parts of Derbyshire. Used by helicopter training from RAF Shawbury and occasional fixed-wing low-level navigation.
lfas.aircraft: Juno HT1, Jupiter HT1, Chinook HC6

dailyFlights.note: Lower-intensity area; mainly student navigation sorties from Shawbury. Fast jet transits are occasional rather than routine.
dailyFlights.sourceLabel: MOD Low Flying Statistics (annual HC Written Answers); RAF Shawbury training statistics

lfas.name: Low Flying Area 14 — Southern England
lfas.description: Covers central-southern England from Wiltshire and Hampshire to Kent. RAF Odiham Chinook operations, Boscombe Down test flying and Lakenheath/Mildenhall transit traffic dominate.
lfas.aircraft: Chinook HC6, Puma HC2, F-35A, F-15E, test aircraft

dailyFlights.note: Includes routine Odiham Chinook training, Boscombe Down test sorties and USAF transit traffic. Activity higher west of the A34 (Hampshire/Wiltshire) than in the east.
dailyFlights.sourceLabel: MOD Low Flying Statistics (annual HC Written Answers); RAF Odiham Environmental Management Plan; QinetiQ/Boscombe Down annual reports

lfas.name: Low Flying Area 19 — Yorkshire Wolds & Holderness
lfas.description: Covers the Yorkshire Wolds, Holderness coast and Humber estuary. Coastal navigation training and approaches to Donna Nook and Cowden weapons ranges.

dailyFlights.note: Activity spikes on range-active days at Donna Nook and Cowden. Quiet on non-range days.
dailyFlights.sourceLabel: MOD Low Flying Statistics (annual HC Written Answers); Donna Nook range activity schedule (published by MOD estates)

corridors.name: RAF Odiham → Salisbury Plain (Chinook Supply Route)
corridors.description: Primary Chinook transit corridor between RAF Odiham and Salisbury Plain Training Area. Documented in RAF Odiham's published Environmental Management Plan and local planning authority consultations. Used daily for army support operations — troop and equipment underslung load lifts. Route hugs the A303 corridor.

corridors.name: RAF Coningsby → Donna Nook (Weapons Range Run)
corridors.description: Direct north-northeast transit used by RAF Coningsby Typhoons for live weapons delivery at Donna Nook Air Weapons Range. Published in Lincolnshire County Council noise assessments and referenced in multiple AIP NOTAMs. Typically 250–500ft AGL along the Lincolnshire coast.

corridors.name: RAF Coningsby → Holbeach (Weapons Range Run)
corridors.description: North transit to Holbeach Air Weapons Range over The Wash foreshore. Published in noise impact studies for RAF Coningsby. Shared with USAF aircraft from Lakenheath and Mildenhall converging on The Wash ranges.

corridors.name: RAF Marham → Holbeach (F-35B Range Transit)
corridors.description: Short direct transit from RAF Marham to Holbeach Air Weapons Range. F-35B Lightning II weapons-delivery practice. Very short corridor (~20mi); aircraft typically climb immediately after range and return low. Referenced in Defence Infrastructure Organisation noise assessment for RAF Marham F-35 conversion.

corridors.name: RAF Lakenheath / Mildenhall → Holbeach (USAF Range Corridor)
corridors.description: USAF range transit used by 48th Fighter Wing F-15Es and F-35As from Lakenheath and 100th ARW KC-135s from Mildenhall. Documented in Suffolk County Council noise planning documents and US Department of the Air Force Environmental Impact Assessments for Lakenheath F-35 beddown.

corridors.name: RAF Coningsby → Spadeadam (EW Training Transit)
corridors.description: Primary transit route for Typhoons travelling to Spadeadam Electronic Warfare Range. Referenced in multiple noise complaint reports and RAF Coningsby's published Environmental Statement. Route climbs out NW, crosses the Pennines at altitude, descends into Spadeadam at low level.
corridors.aircraft: Typhoon FGR4, F-35B, NATO fast jets

corridors.name: RNAS Culdrose → Dartmoor (Estimated)
corridors.description: Estimated Merlin and Wildcat helicopter transit corridor from RNAS Culdrose to Dartmoor Training Area for low-level navigation exercises and live-firing support. Route follows the north Cornish coast before cutting inland over Bodmin Moor. Estimated — not from a published source.

corridors.name: RNAS Yeovilton → Dartmoor (Estimated)
corridors.description: Estimated helicopter transit from RNAS Yeovilton to Dartmoor Training Area (Okehampton ranges). Used by Wildcat and Merlin crews for low-level navigation and simulated close air support with Okehampton garrison troops. Estimated — not from a published source.

corridors.name: RNAS Yeovilton → Salisbury Plain (Estimated)
corridors.description: Estimated transit corridor for Wildcat and Merlin helicopters conducting HELARM (helicopter anti-armour) and close air support training with army units on Salisbury Plain. Yeovilton's F-35B force also transits this route for CAS coordination exercises. Estimated — not from a published source.

corridors.name: RAF Brize Norton → Salisbury Plain (Estimated)
corridors.description: Estimated Chinook and A400M transit corridor from RAF Brize Norton to Salisbury Plain for army logistics support and parachute training (assault drops at DZ Everleigh). Route is short and direct. Estimated — not from a published source.

corridors.name: RAF Benson → Salisbury Plain (Estimated)
corridors.description: Estimated Puma HC2 transit corridor from RAF Benson to Salisbury Plain for army support flying. Very short route (~30mi). Estimated — not from a published source.

corridors.name: RAF Leeming → Otterburn Training Area (Estimated)
corridors.description: Estimated fast jet and helicopter transit from RAF Leeming to Otterburn Training Area for close air support exercises with ground forces. Route crosses the northern Pennines at low level. Estimated — not from a published source.

corridors.name: RAF Leeming → Spadeadam (Estimated)
corridors.description: Estimated transit from RAF Leeming to Spadeadam EW Range for Hawk and Typhoon EW training sorties. Crosses the Stainmore Gap westward into Cumbria. Estimated — not from a published source.

corridors.name: RAF Shawbury → Nesscliffe (Estimated)
corridors.description: Very short estimated helicopter training corridor between RAF Shawbury and Nesscliffe Training Area (~10mi). Used by DHFS Juno and Jupiter students for low-level navigation and confined area landing practice. Estimated — not from a published source.

corridors.name: RAF Honington → Stanford STANTA (Estimated)
corridors.description: Short estimated transit between RAF Honington and Stanford Training Area (STANTA) for RAF Regiment exercises, helicopter insertion and air assault training. Route is near-direct over Breckland heathland. Estimated — not from a published source.
corridors.aircraft: Chinook HC6, Merlin HC4, Wildcat AH1

corridors.name: RAF Lakenheath → Stanford STANTA (Estimated)
corridors.description: Estimated USAF helicopter and tilt-rotor corridor from Lakenheath to Stanford Training Area for USAF Special Operations and ground force integration exercises. Route crosses Breckland. Estimated — not from a published source.

corridors.name: RAF Wittering → Catterick Training Area (Estimated)
corridors.description: Estimated helicopter transit corridor from RAF Wittering northward to Catterick garrison and ranges. Used for support helicopter exercises with armoured formations based at Catterick. Estimated — not from a published source.

corridors.name: RAF Leeming → Warcop (Estimated)
corridors.description: Estimated Hawk and helicopter transit from RAF Leeming to Warcop Training Area in the Eden Valley for live firing support and low-level exercise coordination. Route crosses the northern Pennines via the Stainmore Gap. Estimated — not from a published source.
corridors.aircraft: Hawk T1, Apache AH1, Wildcat AH1

corridors.name: RNAS Culdrose → Plymouth Sound (Estimated)
corridors.description: Estimated Merlin and Wildcat corridor from RNAS Culdrose to Plymouth Sound naval ranges for surface ship gunnery coordination and anti-submarine exercise support. Route follows the south Cornish coast. Estimated — not from a published source.

corridors.name: RAF Coningsby → Cowden Range (Estimated)
corridors.description: Estimated transit from RAF Coningsby to Cowden Air Weapons Range on the Holderness coast. Direct NE route across the Yorkshire Wolds. Estimated — not from a published source.

corridors.name: RAF Northolt → Salisbury Plain (Estimated)
corridors.description: Estimated VIP/government helicopter transit between RAF Northolt and Salisbury Plain for ministerial visits to army garrison headquarters and major exercises. Also used by 32 Squadron for military liaison flights. Estimated — not from a published source.
